headline.commentary: The three major estimates for annual global deaths from fossil-fuel PM2.5 differ by ~2.5x. Vohra et al. use GEOS-Chem chemical transport modelling coupled with newer concentration-response functions; Lelieveld and Burnett use the GBD integrated exposure-response curves. All three agree that fossil-fuel combustion is responsible for ~1 in 5 adult deaths globally from outdoor air pollution.

by_source.notes: Single largest source category. Asia (especially China and India) accounts for >60%% of the total. Both power generation and residential coal heating contribute.
by_source.reference: Vohra et al. 2021, Environmental Research — supplementary Table S2

by_source.notes: Lower per-TWh than coal because gas combustion releases less PM2.5 and fewer SO2/NOx precursors. Still non-zero because of NO2 formation in combustion.
by_source.reference: Vohra et al. 2021, Environmental Research — supplementary Table S2

by_source.notes: Mostly transport (road + shipping + aviation), not power generation. Bunker fuel for shipping is particularly SO2-heavy.
by_source.reference: Vohra et al. 2021, Environmental Research — supplementary Table S2

by_source.notes: Secondary aerosol formation from mixed fossil sources, industrial coke, petrochemical operations. Hard to attribute to a single category.
by_source.reference: Vohra et al. 2021, Environmental Research — supplementary Table S2
